caption:
बॉलीवुड से आई एक बेहद दुखद खबर ने फैंस और पूरी इंडस्ट्री को गहरा झटका दिया है! 💔

'Kaante' और 'Zinda' जैसी दमदार फिल्में बनाने वाले 59 साल के डायरेक्टर Sanjay Gupta अब हमारे बीच नहीं रहे। शुक्रवार रात से शनिवार सुबह के बीच मुंबई स्थित अपने घर पर उन्होंने अंतिम सांस ली।

FWICE चीफ एडवाइजर Ashoke Pandit का दावा है कि सिर में चोट (head injury) लगने से उनका निधन हुआ, हालांकि इस पर कोई ऑफिशियल कन्फर्मेशन नहीं आया है।

पुलिस रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, Versova Police Station में ADR दर्ज कर लिया गया है और जांच चल रही है। पुलिस सूत्रों का कहना है कि फिलहाल किसी साजिश की आशंका नहीं है।

Taran Adarsh ने सोशल मीडिया पर बताया कि वे कुछ दिन पहले ही Sanjay Gupta के घर 'Mata Ki Chowki' में उनसे मिले थे। 1994 में 'Aatish' से करियर शुरू करने वाले डायरेक्टर की सबसे बड़ी हिट 'Kaabil' (₹ 208 crore) थी, वहीं उनकी आखिरी फिल्म 'The Miranda Brothers' JioCinema पर रिलीज हुई थी। 🕯️

Sanjay Gupta की कौन सी फिल्म आपकी सबसे फेवरेट रही है? कमेंट्स में अपनी श्रद्धांजलि दें। 👇

ctx.title: Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta dies at 59; industry mourns Kaante, Shootout at Lokhandwala director
ctx.summary: Director Sanjay Gupta, known for films like Kaante, Shootout at Lokhandwala, and Zinda, has died at the age of 59.
ctx.text:
Director Sanjay Gupta , known for Kaante and Zinda, has died at the age of 59. The news of his death was confirmed by filmmaker and FWICE chief advisor Ashoke Pandit on social media.
The filmmaker died sometime between Friday night and Saturday morning at his home in Mumbai. In his social media post, Ashoke Pandit said the cause of death was a head injury. However, there is no official confirmation yet.
According to sources, an Accidental Death Report (ADR) has been registered at the Versova Police Station, and an investigation is underway. Police sources say no foul play is suspected so far.
As the news of the filmmaker's death flooded social media, members of the film fraternity expressed shock, and offered their tributes.
In a post on Instagram, Ashoke Pandit wrote, “It’s really shocking and sad. Just got the news that our dear friend an ace director Sanjay Gupta is no more. He passed due to a head injury at home. Another talent gone too soon. He was a wonderful narrator, full of life persona & a passionate filmmaker. A great loss to our industry. Will miss you my friend. Condolences to his family & dear ones. Om Shaanti. Details of his last rites will be shared soon.”
Trade analyst and critic Taran Adarsh took to X (formerly Twitter) on Saturday morning and tweeted, “Shocked beyond words... Just can't believe that director #SanjayGupta is no more... Met him just a few days ago at the Mata Ki Chowki held at his residence... This is truly heartbreaking and difficult to process... My deepest condolences to his family... Om Shanti.”
Born in 1967 in Mumbai, Sanjay Gupta began his career at age 26 with the 1994 release, Aatish: The Fire. Over the next few years, he developed expertise in making gangster films, culminating in the 2002 film Kaante. Widely regarded as his best work and one of the best gangster films to come out of Bollywood, it was inspired by Quentin Tarantino's Reservoir Dogs. He followed this up with critically acclaimed and successful films such as Kaante and Shooutout at Lokhandwala. One of his most high-profile films was the Hrithik Roshan-starrer Kaabil, which earned ₹ 208 crore worldwide, emerging as his highest-grosser.
Sanjay Gupta's final directorial was the 2024 sports drama The Miranda Brothers, starring Harshvardhan Rane and Meezaan Jafri. It released on JioCinema.
Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well.

A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism.

Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Film Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day.

Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera).
